name: The AI Video Studio
tagline: Talking-head shorts and claim-checked explainers, planned on a motion board and built as code.
mission: Run a nine-team video studio behind one AI front door. Every edit follows the same loop: a word-timed transcript, a timestamped motion board approved before anything is built, HyperFrames compositions for motion graphics and captions, hard quality gates, and a release package with provenance. Technical statements come from a pinned source and a claim ledger, and a derived cut never asserts more than its source. Publication stays with the owner.

teams.name: Showrunner's Office
teams.purpose: Owns the brief, routes work across the teams, presents the motion board and the final cut to the owner and records the decisions, and keeps the production board current. The owner's own AI is the front door; this office is a stage behind it, not a separate bot.

teams.name: Brand Studio
teams.purpose: Owns the reusable brand kit (type, colour, zones, caption style, motion language) that every production loads by name, and folds lessons from each release back into it.

teams.name: Transcription Desk
teams.purpose: Produces the word-timed transcript for every take (ElevenLabs Scribe or local Whisper), fixes names and terms, reconciles against the script, and publishes words.json as the timing truth.

teams.name: Motion Board Room
teams.purpose: Plans each edit in plan mode: a timestamped motion board with the hook, cuts, every overlay beat with zone, effect, words and claim key, and the caption moves. Nothing is built until it is approved.

teams.name: Motion Graphics Shop
teams.purpose: Builds the approved board as seek-safe HyperFrames compositions: hook cards, animated UI panels, live-typing windows, layer scans and punch-ins, on brand and clear of the face.

teams.name: Captions Desk
teams.purpose: Turns the transcript into short unpunctuated caption phrases, places them in free space away from the face and the overlays, and keeps every caption word traceable to the transcript.

teams.name: Explainer Lab
teams.purpose: Owns scripts, sources and truth: locks each script against a pinned corpus and claim ledger, records or synthesizes the take, and certifies that every cut asserts nothing new.

teams.name: Quality Control
teams.purpose: Gates every cut: lint and check clean, caption trace and style, face-safe placement, hook timing, duration and loudness, claim carryover, and a contact-sheet review against the approved board.

teams.name: Release Desk
teams.purpose: Renders the approved cut and packages the vertical MP4, caption file, cover frame, post copy and provenance. Prepares publication; never performs it.

case.title: Pilot: the WebSocket handshake in 40 seconds
case.brief: Produce the studio's first vertical short (1080x1920, 30 to 45 seconds) from the provided two-voice script about how a WebSocket connection starts. Record it as a talking head or synthesize it for a faceless layout. Open on the question hook, show the HTTP Upgrade request as a live-typing window and the 101 answer as an animated UI panel, caption every spoken word in short unpunctuated phrases, keep every on-screen technical statement traceable to RFC 6455 through the claim ledger, and hand over a release-ready package. Nothing is uploaded or published.
success_criteria: A 1080x1920 H.264 MP4 of 30 to 45 seconds renders from a clean checkout with a pinned HyperFrames CLI, and lint and check report zero errors.
The hook is on screen by 0.5 seconds, holds at least 2.5 seconds, and matches the approved motion board.
Every caption word traces to the take's words.json in order; phrases have one to four words and no punctuation, and none enters the face zone or the platform-safe areas.
Every on-screen technical statement maps to a verified claim whose anchor matches the pinned RFC 6455 bytes; nothing new is asserted.
The motion board was approved before the build started, and PROVENANCE.json records the script, claim ledger, corpus, board and approval hashes, the project commit and the CLI version.
No upload, publication or other external effect occurs.

tasks.title: Write the production brief
tasks.instructions: Turn the case into BRIEF.md: audience, platform, 30 to 45 second target, the hook, the source option (talking head or synthesized), the kit, the gates and who signs each, and what is out of scope.
acceptance: Names the hook, the target length, the source option and the kit.
States that publication is out of scope.

tasks.title: Lock the script against the claim ledger
tasks.instructions: Fetch the pinned RFC 6455 text, confirm its sha256, confirm every claim anchor's snippet sits inside its line range, and confirm every factual script line maps to a verified claim. Record the script and ledger sha256.
acceptance: The corpus sha256 matches source/corpus.json.
Every anchor verifies and every factual line has a verified claim key.
Records the sha256 of script.md and claims.json.

tasks.title: Issue the house kit
tasks.instructions: Resolve the house kit for this production: download the OFL fonts with their licences, confirm zones for the chosen layout (talking head, or source card in place of the face zone), and issue design.md and tokens.json. Run tools/check-kit.mjs.
acceptance: check-kit.mjs passes on the issued kit.
Every font is a licensed file with its licence text.

tasks.title: Record or synthesize the take
tasks.instructions: Record the locked script to camera (vertical, 30 fps, clean close-mic audio, written consent from everyone on camera), or synthesize the two voices with a voice licensed for publication. Record media path, sha256, duration and capture notes.
acceptance: The take speaks the locked script; deviations are listed.
Records sha256, duration, layout option, and consent or voice licence.

tasks.title: Publish the word-timed transcript
tasks.instructions: Transcribe the take with tools/transcribe.mjs, fix terms, reconcile against the script with --known, and publish words.json and transcript.txt on the source timeline.
acceptance: Word times are monotonic and inside the take.
Script agreement is reported; terms such as Sec-WebSocket-Key are spelled as in the script.
Records the engine, model and settings.

tasks.title: Plan the motion board
tasks.instructions: In plan mode, write the timestamped motion board: the hook in the first three seconds, cuts in silence, one row per overlay with zone, effect, on-screen words, claim key and reference image, and where captions move.
acceptance: Beats cover the whole cut without two overlays in one zone at once.
Every technical overlay cites a claim key.
No beat is placed in the face zone or the platform-safe areas.

tasks.title: Present the motion board and record the decision
tasks.instructions: Check the board against the brief, present it to the owner, and record the owner's decision with the board sha256, or return it with specific, testable changes. Building starts only after an approval record exists.
acceptance: Records the decision, the reviewer and the board sha256.

tasks.title: Build the spatial captions
tasks.instructions: Run tools/caption-phraser.mjs on the transcript with the issued kit and the board's cuts, place phrases in the caption zone, move them where the board says an overlay owns that zone, and verify the trace.
acceptance: caption-phraser.mjs --verify passes.
No caption overlaps the face zone, the platform-safe areas or an active overlay.

tasks.title: Build the overlays and assemble the cut
tasks.instructions: Create the HyperFrames project, cut the take, build each board beat from the starter overlays and the effect catalogue, wire the captions, and keep lint and check clean.
acceptance: short.json lists every overlay with its board beat and zone.
lint and check report zero errors.
The hook overlay is on screen by 0.5 seconds.

tasks.title: Certify claim carryover
tasks.instructions: Map every on-screen technical statement in the cut to a verified claim key and anchor. Anything unmapped is a new claim: return it instead of certifying.
acceptance: Zero unmapped on-screen statements.

tasks.title: Run the quality gates
tasks.instructions: Walk the review checklist: lint, check, duration, hook, caption trace and style, zones, claim carryover, loudness, and a contact sheet with one frame per beat compared against the approved board.
acceptance: Every checklist row has a pass or a documented fail with evidence.
The contact sheet shows one frame per board beat.

tasks.title: Present the final cut and record the decision
tasks.instructions: Present the QC report and contact sheet to the owner and record the decision with the project commit, or return the cut with specific notes.
acceptance: Records the decision, the reviewer and the project commit.

tasks.title: Render and package the deliverables
tasks.instructions: Render the approved commit from a clean checkout, export the SRT and a cover frame, draft the post copy, and write PROVENANCE.json. Prepare only: do not upload or publish.
acceptance: The MP4 is 1080x1920 H.264 between 30 and 45 seconds.
PROVENANCE.json records every hash the case requires.
Nothing was uploaded or published.

tasks.title: Fold the lessons back into the kit
tasks.instructions: Read the QC report and provenance and propose concrete kit changes (caption style, zones, motion defaults, prompts) as a reviewed diff for the next production.
acceptance: Each proposed change cites the QC finding behind it.
